### 2.9 BEANS (beans)

`data/benchmarks/audio-speech/beans.yaml` · `verification_status: ai-drafted-unverified` · curator confidence medium · added 2026-11-05 · last verified 2026-11-05

*Earth Species Project's ten public animal-sound datasets, five for classification and five for window-level detection.*

A collection of public bioacoustics datasets, each with fixed train, validation and test splits, released in 2022 by Earth Species Project to measure machine-learning methods across species. Five datasets are single-label classification, scored by accuracy: marine mammal species (Watkins), Egyptian fruit bat individuals, 264 North American bird species from the Cornell Bird Identification competition (split so that no recordist is in two splits), individual domestic dogs from their barks, and mosquito species from wingbeat sound (HumBugDB). Five are detection: long recordings cut into 1-minute chunks and then into sliding windows, each window labelled with every species or call type it overlaps, scored by mean average precision (DCASE 2021 Task 5's bird and mammal recordings, an eastern North American dawn chorus, minke whale "boings" from the HICEAS survey, tropical birds and frogs from Rainforest Connection, Hainan gibbon calls). ESC-50 and Speech Commands are included as auxiliary datasets that are not officially part of the benchmark. The paper asks users not to average across datasets and tasks. Its baselines (logistic regression to gradient-boosted trees on MFCC statistics, ResNets and VGGish, fine-tuned per dataset) leave most datasets well below 90%. A repository downloads, re-splits and validates the data and runs the baselines; there is no leaderboard, and results appear in papers, where bioacoustic encoders are now usually compared with frozen weights and a trained probe.

#### beans · Domain and capabilities

- `domain` = primary audio-speech/bioacoustics; secondary earth-climate/ecology-biodiversity · [S2][beans-s2]
  - why: Every official dataset scores identifying species, individuals or call types from recordings of animal sound, the leaf's definition. The benchmark is single-modality and its claim is machine-learning method for bioacoustics, which ecology-biodiversity's exclusion test sends to this leaf with ecology secondary; the secondary carries the species-monitoring purpose. Ecology was weighed as primary. Passive acoustic monitoring and conservation motivate the paper, but it is a method benchmark in one modality, not a biodiversity suite across modalities as LifeCLEF is, and that term's not\_to\_be\_confused\_with puts this case under bioacoustics.
  > Here, we propose BEANS (the BEnchmark of ANimal Sounds), a collection of bioacoustics tasks and public datasets, specifically designed to measure the performance of machine learning algorithms in the field of bioacoustics.
- `capability` = perception · [S2][beans-s2]
  - why: Every task starts from a recording and is scored on what was recovered from it, a species, an individual, a call type, or the labels present in a window.
  > The benchmark proposed here consists of two common tasks in bioacoustics: classification and detection.
- `evaluation_method` = exact-match, classification-metric · [S1][beans-s1]
  - why: The five classification datasets are scored by plain accuracy over a fixed label set (exact-match). The five detection datasets are scored by mean average precision, the 11-point interpolated precision-recall area of each class's window scores, averaged over classes, with no IoU sweep (classification-metric).
  > and auxiliary tasks, and mean average precision (mAP) for detection tasks
- `designed_for_subjects` = domain-specialist-model · [S1][beans-s1]
  - why: The intended entrants are models trained or fine-tuned for bioacoustic identification, species, individuals and call types, tasks that zoology and ecology define, and the paper wants generic bioacoustic models across species; current users enter bioacoustic encoders pretrained on animal sound (AVES, BirdAVES, NatureBEATs). The same reading put LifeCLEF's entrants under this term.
  > Such models are of interest to the bioacoustic community due to better generalizability and lower development cost.

**Open review checks** (10):

1. (field `data.size`) The headline count. The abstract says 12 datasets, but two of them (ESC-50, Speech Commands) are auxiliary and not officially part of the benchmark. size leads with the ten and the auxiliary pair is its own subset group; a reviewer may prefer 12 as the headline. · [S1][beans-s1]
   > but benchmark users can choose to report performance numbers on them as a reference
2. (field `data.access`) data.access gated-registration rests on cbi and rfcx coming only through Kaggle accounts and competition rules. If BEANS-Zero's ungated Hugging Face copy of their test items counted as an official copy, the data would be fully-open, but it is another benchmark's instruction-formatted, test-only set. The dogs data's "academic use by personal correspondence" was not tested, and the October 2024 change of file hosts was read only from the commit list. · [S5][beans-s5]
   > The benchmark also relies on a few Kaggle datasets.
3. (field `designed_for_subjects`) designed\_for\_subjects domain-specialist-model treats species and individual identification from animal sound as a biological discipline's task, as LifeCLEF's entry does. The taxonomy puts bioacoustics under audio-speech, which could argue for task-specific-supervised-model, the term the paper's own general-architecture baselines fit.
4. (field `as_used`) Designed against used. The paper fine-tunes each whole network per dataset; current use probes frozen encoders, and the May 2026 paper finds that probe choice moves encoder rankings. The facets follow the design; the protocol difference sits in as\_used and in comparability (training\_data\_policy, harness), and there is no field for the probe. · [S3][beans-s3]
   > Most bioacoustic benchmarks use a fixed, low-capacity probe, such as a linear layer on the final encoder layer.
5. (field `aggregation_policy`) aggregation\_policy none-by-design follows the paper, but users report averages over each task group (the May 2026 paper); whether the catalogue should record that as the dominant reported number. · [S3][beans-s3]
   > We split the results for BEANS into classification and detection.
6. (field `lineage`) Lineage. BEANS-Zero and BEANS-Next are taken as separate benchmarks linked as variants (different items, entrants and releases, same maintainer). Whether BEANS-Next supersedes BEANS-Zero, and whether either should instead hang from the other, is for their own entries; the BEANS-Next PDF was not read. · [S10][beans-s10]
   > primarily centered on label-centric biological category recognition, such as species and call-type classification
7. (field `lifecycle`) lifecycle active rests on the maintainer's May 2026 paper and on one outside paper (BioMamba, v2 April 2026) read only as its abstract. The repository has not changed since October 2024, which is maintenance evidence.
8. (field `data.dataset_licence`) The per-dataset licences, items and label counts are read from Table 1, which the PDF text flattens column by column; each was matched to its dataset by the table's order and checked against BEANS-Zero's card where it repeats them. Two disagreements remain unresolved (gibbons CC-NC-SA in Table 1, CC-BY-NC-SA on the card), and the text says HICEAS was downsampled to 22.5 kHz where the table lists 500 kHz, the source rate. · [S1][beans-s1]
   > CC-BY CC0 freed freee CC-NC-SA
9. (field `release_venue`) release\_venue ICASSP 2023 comes from a citing paper's reference list; the ICASSP version and its DOI were not read, so paper.doi is null.
10. (field `governance.independence_flags`) maintainer-competes-on-own-benchmark is set on Earth Species Project's own encoders (NatureBEATs, AVES) scored on BEANS in its own papers; with no leaderboard the flag has less weight than on a ranked benchmark.

### 2.10 BirdSet (birdset)

`data/benchmarks/audio-speech/birdset.yaml` · `verification_status: ai-drafted-unverified` · curator confidence medium · added 2026-11-05 · last verified 2026-11-05

*Bird species in 5-second soundscape segments from eight sites, after training on 528k Xeno-canto focal recordings.*

A benchmark dataset collection for audio classification in avian bioacoustics, from the DBD research group (the Deep Bird Detect project; University of Kassel, Kiel University and Fraunhofer IEE), published at ICLR 2025. Training data is a curated snapshot of Xeno-canto, the citizen-science platform for bird recordings: 528,434 focal recordings of 9,734 species (XCL), a 409-species subset covering the test sets (XCM), and a dedicated subset for each test set. Evaluation uses fully annotated passive acoustic monitoring soundscapes from eight project sites, released earlier on Zenodo by their own authors: seven test sets (Amazon Basin, Colombia and Costa Rica, Hawai'i, High Sierra Nevada, NIPS4BPlus, Sapsucker Woods, Sierra Nevada) and Powdermill for validation. Each soundscape is cut into 5-second segments labelled from the annotation timestamps, and a model scores every species in a segment; the paper reports class-mean average precision, AUROC and top-1 accuracy per test set and averaged over them, in three training scenarios (large on XCL, medium on XCM, dedicated fine-tuning). Training on focal recordings and testing on soundscapes builds a covariate and task shift into every result. Data and a codebase are on Hugging Face and GitHub, with a Hugging Face leaderboard Space that holds only the maintainers' baselines and Perch. Five of the test sets were BirdCLEF test data in 2019-2022.

#### birdset · Domain and capabilities

- `domain` = primary audio-speech/bioacoustics; secondary earth-climate/ecology-biodiversity · [S1][birdset-s1]
  - why: The scored task is identifying bird species from field-recorded audio, the bioacoustics leaf's definition, and the benchmark's own claim is audio classification, one method in one modality. ecology-biodiversity's exclusion test sends a single species-call task scored as audio to bioacoustics with ecology secondary, as the family's birdclef-plus example does; the paper ties the task to biodiversity monitoring.
  > The primary task in avian bioacoustics is the multi-label classification in PAM, comparable to classification in AudioSet.
- `capability` = perception · [S1][birdset-s1]
  - why: The input is a soundscape segment's audio and the score measures which species were recovered from it.
  > Each segment is an independent test sample containing none (0-vector), one or multiple species.
- `capability` = distribution-shift-generalization · [S1][birdset-s1]
  - why: Models train on focal recordings (directional microphone, one bird) and are scored only on passive soundscapes from eight held-out sites, with each test set reported on its own. The species label set is unchanged; the inputs move.
  > This gap is particularly pronounced in avian bioacoustics due to the use of focals for training and soundscapes for testing.
- `evaluation_method` = classification-metric · [S1][birdset-s1]
  - why: Class-mean average precision, AUROC and top-1 accuracy over each test set's segments, all threshold-free statistics of the score ranking against the segment labels, with no IoU sweep.
  > We use threshold-free metrics to assess generalization without threshold-tuning
- `designed_for_subjects` = domain-specialist-model · [S1][birdset-s1]
  - why: The intended entrants are bird-sound classifiers trained on the benchmark's Xeno-canto sets (large, medium or dedicated) or bioacoustic models such as Perch, a task defined by avian ecology, a discipline in the earth-climate family; general audio models (AST, EAT, Wav2Vec2) enter only after training on the bird data.
  > In large training (LT) and medium training (MT), we train models on XCL and XCM, respectively.

**Open review checks** (9):

1. (field `lineage`) Relation to BirdCLEF (lifeclef). Five of BirdSet's seven test sets were BirdCLEF test data (PER and HSN 2020, NES and SNE 2021, UHH 2022, SSW 2019-2021), taken from their Zenodo releases, and a BirdSet co-author leads the BirdCLEF overviews. BirdSet presents itself as a fixed-protocol complement to the yearly competition, not an edition of it, so it is a separate benchmark with no lineage link; lifeclef's versions start in 2024, so nothing there shares items with BirdSet. A reviewer may want a correlates\_with or a note on lifeclef. · [S1][birdset-s1]
   > complementing BirdCLEF as a foundation for future challenges
2. (field `domain`) Primary domain. bioacoustics with ecology-biodiversity secondary, by ecology's own exclusion test (one audio method task) and birdclef-plus's example. The paper's claim is broader audio classification, which argued for audio-event-understanding; it lost to the species labels. · [S1][birdset-s1]
   > This serves as a crucial application since fluctuations in bird populations indicate broader shifts in biodiversity
3. (field `activity`) activity closed rests on the Space's runtime error and a results dataset unchanged since 2024-09-30, with the README still inviting submissions and no stated pause. unknown (the board could not be read) and accepting-submissions (the invitation stands) were weighed; a reviewer who finds the Space running again should make it accepting-submissions. · [S6][birdset-s6]
   > by submitting new results and comparing performance across models
4. (field `data.dataset_licence`) The dataset licence disagrees between sources. The Hugging Face repository says CC BY-NC 4.0; the paper says CC BY-NC-SA, with test sets CC BY 4.0 and validation CC0. The entry takes the repository's declaration. · [S1][birdset-s1]
   > is available under the creative commons (CC) CC-BY-NC-SA license
5. (field `as_used`) Perch 2.0 describes BirdSet as six datasets and its table lists PER, NES, UHH, HSN, NBP and SSW, while the paper has seven test sets (SNE included). Averages from the two are not over the same sets; recorded in as\_used and comparability (subset\_used). · [S3][birdset-s3]
   > consists of six fully-annotated datasets from the continental United States
6. (field `designed_for_subjects`) designed\_for\_subjects domain-specialist-model treats avian species identification as a discipline's task (ecology), as lifeclef's BirdCLEF+ did; the paper's framing as general audio classification would argue for task-specific-supervised-model.
7. (field `versions`) No versions are recorded. The paper went through six arXiv versions under three titles (v1 'A Multi-Task Benchmark', v3 'A Dataset and Benchmark', v4 on 'A Large-Scale Dataset'), and the dataset card logs three revisions (taxonomy metadata, a download fix, a loader update). The test sets are stated to be fixed; whether v1-v3 scored the same test sets or metrics was not read. · [S9][birdset-s9]
   > Additional bird taxonomy metadata, including "Genus," "Species Group," and "Order," is provided using the 2021 eBird taxonomy
8. (field `headline_metric`) The headline is left null. The paper reports cmAP, AUROC and top-1 accuracy side by side and the leaderboard shows all three; Perch 2.0 argues AUROC is the most stable. A reviewer could set AUROC. · [S3][birdset-s3]
   > Although the BirdSet benchmark calculates several scores, we believe that the ROC-AUC score is the most stable and informative
9. (field `lineage`) Relation to BEANS (drafted in parallel). The paper sets BirdSet against BEANS as a larger, multi-label, bird-only benchmark, and Perch 2.0 reports both; they share no test data in the sources read. · [S1][birdset-s1]
   > While BEANS covers various animal sounds, it lacks volume
